purpose: Anastrozole is used to treat breast cancer in women who have gone through menopause. It is often used after surgery or other cancer treatments to help keep the cancer from coming back. It may also be used to treat breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body.
how_it_works: Your body makes a hormone called estrogen, and some breast cancers use estrogen to grow. Anastrozole works by blocking an enzyme called aromatase, which your body needs to produce estrogen. By lowering estrogen levels in your body, this medicine helps slow down or stop the growth of certain breast cancer cells.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes, joint pain or stiffness, muscle aches, feeling tired or weak, headache, nausea, bone pain, mood changes, and trouble sleeping. Some people also notice thinning hair or dry skin.
warnings: This medicine can weaken your bones over time, raising your risk of osteoporosis and fractures, so your doctor may monitor your bone density. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or could become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially estrogen-containing products or tamoxifen, as they can interfere with how this medicine works. Let your doctor know right away if you notice unusual bone pain, chest pain, or severe mood changes.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 1 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Treatment often continues for several years, so follow your doctor's instructions carefully and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
